correctness.rationale: From Weibull profile scale MLE, sum Y_i=n. For all t≤1/n the empirical minCF is exactly t; the null Exp(1) minCF equals t(1-exp(-1/t)), forcing the deterministic square term. An explicit integrable tail bound and Bessel/Laplace saddle prove uniform first-order collapse. The clipping decomposition isolates the max breakpoint t=1/M, with linear slope rM/n; endpoint Watson expansion gives correction 2r exp(-M-gamma/M)/gamma². For unequal maxima, exponential rate comparison proves eventual reverse ordering. The current package checker passed 66 high-precision assertions (not itself the infinite proof).

value.rationale: For the published exponential-weight Weibull minCF statistic, the large-tuning limit discards all sample dependence at the dominant Bessel scale; the first surviving information is an exponentially smaller maximum-order correction that reverses the conventional large-statistic ordering. The explicit nonasymptotic bound and joint gamma/n² regime quantify the weight/sample-size relationship and explain when numeric calibration becomes extremely delicate. This is a motivated structural boundary for a specific test, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a mere restatement of consistency.
